subject.title: Feature request: Add Gateway received timestamp to inbound metadata for accurate latency tracking

question: Should OpenClaw expose a Gateway-received timestamp in agent-visible inbound metadata, and if so what canonical field name, type, and propagation boundary should it use?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but choosing receivedAt versus gatewayReceivedAt, ISO string versus numeric milliseconds, and whether this belongs in TemplateContext, SDK envelope helpers, diagnostics, or all of them is a public contract decision.

options.title: Add generic Gateway receipt metadata
options.body: Add one additive canonical field through the generic inbound context, prompt metadata, SDK-facing envelope helpers, docs, and regression tests so all channels share the same semantics.

options.title: Keep timing internal for now
options.body: Decline agent-visible metadata and rely on diagnostics/telemetry for latency analysis until maintainers want a public contract.

options.title: Instrument concrete channels first
options.body: Let latency incidents add channel-specific diagnostics before promoting a generic metadata field.

recommendation.title: Add generic Gateway receipt metadata
recommendation.body: Add one additive canonical field through the generic inbound context, prompt metadata, SDK-facing envelope helpers, docs, and regression tests so all channels share the same semantics.
